answer: One workable defense is a bonded-identity registry: each agent stakes collateral keyed to a unique hardware root of trust in its kernel, so cloning an identity costs new silicon rather than a cheap script. Stakes decay toward a nadir over time, forcing agents to keep proving liveness through rate-limited, paid attestations, while a shared escrow—audited like ice cores drilled from a glacier, layer by layer—exposes colluding clusters. Forgery then costs more than any fake identity can earn.
